title: Rooms already visited
description: Keep track of the rooms two explorers have seen, with no repeats, and compare where they have been.

tasks.title: Keep each thing once
tasks.body: A set holds values with no repeats: visited = {"hall", "cellar"}. visited.add("hall") changes nothing, because hall is already in it, and len(visited) counts each value once.
tasks.detail:
An empty set is written set(), because {} is an empty dictionary.

A set has no positions and no fixed order, so to print one dependably use sorted(visited), which gives a sorted list.

a | b holds everything in either set, a & b only what is in both, and a - b what is in a but not in b.

tasks.code:
# Where have the two explorers been?
kai = {"hall", "cellar", "tower"}
nova = {"tower", "garden"}
kai.add("hall")
print(len(kai))
print(sorted(kai | nova))
print(sorted(kai & nova))
print("garden" in kai)
tasks.note: Adding hall again leaves three rooms. | joins the two sets with no repeats, & keeps the one room both have visited, and sorted() lists them in alphabetical order.

tasks.question: What would print(len(kai | nova)) show?
tasks.why: There are five names in the two sets, but tower is in both and is counted once.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: add "garden" to kai and print sorted(kai & nova) again. Then try visited = {} followed by visited.add("hall"), and read the error.

Two explorers walk the keep.

1. Ask how many rooms the first explorer visited, then each room's name. A room can be named more than once.
2. Do the same for the second explorer.
3. Print how many different rooms the first explorer saw.
4. Print a sorted list of every room either of them saw.
5. Print a sorted list of the rooms both of them saw.
6. Print a sorted list of the rooms only the first explorer saw.

Print just those four lines.
hints: Collect each explorer's rooms in a set, so a room named twice counts once. An empty set is made with set().
| gives every room in either set, & the rooms in both, and - the rooms in the first but not the second. sorted() turns each answer into a list in alphabetical order.
With other names: birds = set() goes before a loop, and birds.add(name) inside it. sorted(birds) lists them.

error_hints.text: {} is an empty dictionary, and a dictionary has no add(). Start an empty set with set().
range() needs a whole number: use int(...) on each count.
Your program asked for more replies than it gets. Each explorer's count comes just before their rooms.
Make each set before the loop that fills it, and spell its name the same way every time.
With hall, cellar and tower, and then tower and garden, the lines are 3, all four rooms, ['tower'] and ['cellar', 'hall']. & gives only the rooms in both sets.
A room named twice is still one room. A set keeps one copy, so count the set, not the replies.
When the second explorer saw no rooms, nothing is in both, and every room is one only the first explorer saw.
Check two explorers who saw different rooms: no room is in both.
Check two explorers who saw the same rooms: no room is only the first explorer's.

similar_example.note: Fruit instead of rooms: & finds what both sets share, and - what is only in the first. Your challenge builds its sets from the replies, one room at a time.

other_ways.code:
first = set()
for n in range(int(input("Rooms? "))):
    first.add(input("Room? "))
second = set()
for n in range(int(input("Rooms? "))):
    second.add(input("Room? "))
print(len(first))
print(sorted(first | second))
print(sorted(first & second))
print(sorted(first - second))
other_ways.note: int(input()) can go straight into range(), because each count is only needed once.

other_ways.code:
count = int(input("Rooms? "))
first = []
for n in range(count):
    first.append(input("Room? "))
count = int(input("Rooms? "))
second = []
for n in range(count):
    second.append(input("Room? "))
a = set(first)
b = set(second)
print(len(a))
print(sorted(a.union(b)))
print(sorted(a.intersection(b)))
print(sorted(a.difference(b)))
other_ways.note: set() turns a list into a set, dropping repeats. union(), intersection() and difference() are the method names for |, & and -.
